pensamiento:
I'm checking BAN-06 against the QUS criteria. The story is about a branch cashier wanting to see an account's available balance in real time, so they can answer the customer without calling another department. It looks fine on the first three checks: the format is right, it covers a single objective, and it has no extra notes. I'm now reviewing the benefit clause in QUS-004.

I'm going through the rest of the QUS and INV checks on BAN-06. The benefit clause, tech neutrality, and the "en tiempo real" wording all pass, since the 2-second acceptance criterion gives that phrase a measure. I'm now asking whether the story is estimable, because the invalid-account case, the account types, and the core integration are not covered yet.

I'm now weighing DOR-002 and DOR-001 for BAN-06. The acceptance criteria only cover the valid-account path, so the invalid account, blocked account, and unavailable core cases are undefined, which is a clear defect. The dependency on the core balance service is implied but never named.

I'm now checking the dependency side for BAN-06: the balance has to come from the core, and the cashier needs a channel such as the terminal application to reach it, yet neither source is named, so DOR-001 is a defect. The non-functional requirement is covered, since the 2-second limit sits in the acceptance criteria, so DOR-003 passes. I'll look at size next to set an estimate and check whether the criterion is verifiable.

Both DOR-001 and DOR-002 are defects here, so the story goes back. I'll leave INV-003 alone, and I'm treating "tiempo real" as acceptable since the 2-second criterion makes it measurable. Next I'll run the estimation tools for the record.
